page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance built on x86_64 architecture using AMD EPYC 7T83 processors. It features 32 physical cores delivering 64 dedicated vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 2.55 GHz, paired with 128 GB of RAM to maintain a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Cache allocation includes 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 16 Gbps. The instance includes no bundled local NVMe SSD storage or GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage for persistent volumes.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong multi-core execution capabilities, evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core CPU result of 86349.63 and a PassMark CPU score of 59199.92, placing in the top 25% tier. Encryption throughput and PassMark database operations also reach top-quartile performance, while Redis SET operations achieve 61.81 million operations per second. Small-model LLM inference prompt processing and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression show similar upper-quartile speed. Conversely, uncached memory bandwidth over large block sizes and Geekbench multi-core scores remain within average benchmark ranges.

The heavy vCPU allocation relative to system memory provides high resource density for parallel compute tasks without incurring cost for unused RAM. Tradeoffs include the absence of local ephemeral storage and lack of AVX-512 vector extensions. This infrastructure profile fits distributed compilation pipelines, Redis key-value caching layers, batch data transformations, and microservice orchestration.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized cloud instance powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at 2.55 GHz. It equips 32 physical cores and 64 dedicated vCPUs paired with 128 GB of memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio tailored for parallel execution. The system features 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, while omitting bundled local storage and GPU hardware. Hardware benchmark results indicate strong multi-core compute capability, highlighted by high stress-ng CPU execution, elevated Redis operation throughput at 61.81 million SETs per second, and upper-quartile PassMark database and encryption scores. Uncached memory bandwidth and Geekbench scores fall into the average range. The server offers dense CPU processing power without the overhead of excess memory, providing efficient qualitative economics for multithreaded workloads, software compilation, data transformations, and high-concurrency caching tiers.
